newsitem.title: USA: US Senate vote on Barshefsky next week at earliest.
newsitem.headline: US Senate vote on Barshefsky next week at earliest.

text.p: The Senate Finance Committee will not file Charlene Barshefsky's nomination for U.S. Trade Representative with the Senate clerk until she has answered written questions, a panel spokeswoman said Thursday.
The nomination must be filed with the clerk before the full Senate can vote on it.
The committee approved Barshefsky's nomination Thursday. Members of the committee submitted written questions after Barshefsky's confirmation hearing Wednesday.
"We are waiting for the USTR to do all the answers to the written questions that were submitted," the spokeswoman said.
After the answers are received, the committee will file Barshefsky's nomination with the Senate clerk, and then a full Senate vote can be scheduled.
The Senate is not in session Friday, so the earliest the nomination could go to the clerk would be next week, the spokeswoman said.

The committee Thursday also voted in favor of a waiver of a 1995 law that prevents those who have worked for foreign governments from holding the post. As a private attorney, Barshefsky advised Canada in 1990 on a lumber dispute with the United States.
While the nomination needs approval only from the Senate, the waiver must be approved by the Senate and House of Representatives.
